Wave Management: Push, Freeze and Crash

Control where the minion wave sits in your lane, and you control when fights happen, how safe you are, and how much gold your opponent gets.

Why waves matter

Minion waves are the heartbeat of every lane. Where the wave sits decides who is safe, who can be ganked, who can roam, and who loses gold. Two players with the same mechanics can have very different games just because one of them moves the wave on purpose and the other just hits whatever is in front of them.

The basic rule: the side with more minions pushes. If your wave has more minions (or stronger ones, like a cannon), it kills the enemy wave and walks toward their tower. Every time you kill an enemy minion, you change that balance. Wave management is simply choosing how fast you kill minions to put the wave where you want it.

Waves arrive every 30 seconds early on, then every 25 seconds from 14:00 and every 20 seconds from 30:00. The first cannon comes on wave 3 (1:30), then every third wave until 14:00, every second wave until 25:00, and every wave after that. Cannon waves push harder, so plan around them.

The five wave states

TechniqueHowUse it when
Fast pushKill the wave as quickly as you can with abilities and attacks.You want to recall, roam, help at an objective, or you need to get to the tower before your opponent.
Slow pushOnly last-hit, or kill just the enemy casters first, and let your wave build up over 2-3 waves.You want a huge wave to crash into the tower, often before a recall or a dive.
CrashPush a big wave all the way into the enemy tower.Right before you recall or roam, so your opponent has to farm under tower and loses minions.
FreezeKeep the wave just outside your own tower range by only last-hitting, with a few more enemy minions than yours.You're ahead or your opponent is weak, and you want them to walk forward to farm.
BounceAfter you crash a wave, the tower kills your minions and the next wave pushes back to you.Naturally happens after a crash. Time your recall so you come back as the wave arrives.
Pro tipKill the enemy caster minions first when you want to slow push. They have low health and deal the most damage to your minions, so removing them lets your wave win the fight slowly and pile up.

How to freeze

A freeze is the most powerful wave state for a player who is ahead. You hold the wave close to your tower, so your opponent has to walk deep into your side of the map to get gold and experience. That means they're far from safety and easy to gank.

  1. The wave needs to be meeting near your tower, but outside of its range. If the tower hits the enemy minions, the freeze breaks.
  2. Keep a few more enemy minions than allied ones (about 3-4 extra caster minions is a good amount). If the numbers are even, the wave drifts toward you.
  3. Only last-hit. Don't use abilities on minions, and don't auto-attack minions that aren't about to die.
  4. If the enemy wave gets too big, kill a few extra enemy minions to keep it from pushing into tower range.

Freezes are easier to hold when you're the bigger threat. If your opponent can walk up and fight you for free, they'll just push the wave out of the freeze.

Crashing before you recall

The cleanest way to recall is: push the wave, crash it into the enemy tower, then recall. While you're shopping, the enemy has to clear your minions under their tower (where they can't trade or roam freely), and you'll come back as the wave bounces back toward you. You lose almost nothing.

Recalling with the wave pushing toward you is the opposite: your minions die to the enemy wave, the enemy wave crashes into your tower, and you lose gold and experience. Turret plates don't fall off any more in 2026, so a big wave hitting your tower while you're gone can also cost your team plates for the rest of the game.

Common mistakeRecalling with a big enemy wave about to hit your tower. Even if your health is low, it's often worth spending 10 more seconds to push the wave first, unless you're in danger of dying.

Cannon waves and timing

Cannon minions have lots of health and deal strong damage, so a cannon wave pushes harder than a normal one. That makes cannon waves great waves to crash. If you're slow pushing, try to let the cannon wave be the one that hits the tower.

Cannon minions are also worth the most gold of any minion (50 gold, growing slowly over the game). Never miss them for a trade. A common trick is to time big trades or all-ins for the moment your opponent goes to last-hit the cannon, because they have to walk forward and use an attack on it.

Later in the game, cannons come every second wave (from 14:00) and then every wave (from 25:00), so waves get much stronger. A late-game wave can take a tower on its own, which is why side lanes matter so much. See Side Lanes & Split Pushing.

Choosing the right technique

  • You won a trade and your opponent is low: fast push and crash, then recall or pressure their tower.
  • You're losing the lane: let the wave come to you. Farm under your tower and avoid fights.
  • You're ahead: freeze to deny gold, or crash and roam to spread your lead.
  • An objective is spawning soon: push your wave first so you can move without losing minions. Read Objectives: Dragons, Grubs, Herald and Baron.
  • Your jungler is coming to gank: having the wave on your side of the lane makes ganks much easier, because the enemy has further to run.

Key takeaways

  • The side with more minions pushes. Every minion you kill changes where the wave goes.
  • Crash the wave into the enemy tower before you recall or roam.
  • Freeze outside your tower range when you're ahead to make your opponent walk into danger.
  • Slow push by killing caster minions first to build a big wave.
  • Cannon waves push harder and are worth the most gold. Plan around them.
